original_ai_prompt:
We're a four-doctor clinic opening a new premises. I need the network designed with clear separation, because patient information must not be reachable from waiting areas.

- Reception and admin PCs (about 6) handle bookings and records.
- Consulting rooms have a wired PC each (4 rooms).
- The waiting area has a shared kiosk PC (1) that patients can use.
- Patient/consulting traffic must be separate from the waiting area.
- The records server hosts the clinic's HTTP page and DNS, so it gets a fixed address; everything else is automatic addressing.

We have a WAN handoff from the ISP for internet. We're not doing patient WiFi yet, so the kiosk stays wired for now.

requirements.statement: Admin, clinical and waiting/guest are separate networks
Patient/consulting traffic is not reachable from the waiting area
The records server is statically addressed
A records server with HTTP and DNS exists

expected_behaviour: Three VLANs, static records server (http+dns) on the clinical VLAN, WAN internet. The patient-facing access is the wired waiting kiosk (no wireless isolation claim), so this builds.
capability_limitations: Three VLANs, static records server (http+dns) on the clinical VLAN, WAN internet. The patient-facing access is the wired waiting kiosk (no wireless isolation claim), so this builds.
why_suitable: Healthcare realism (patient-data separation) mapped into a shape the engine can actually build; demonstrates research -> original scenario -> validation.
